scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The Internet Lab has DISAPPEARED for the whole
Office department!! All morning none of the 128.168.0.x machines answer any of
our PCs, the 192.168.3.x ones -- everything else works, it's just the lab
that's gone. Something around the link that carries us over to the Internet
Lab must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the connection
and get us back to their machines? We need them TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claims that the Office department (192.168.3.x) has lost all
connectivity to the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x), but every diagnostic layer
examined contradicts this claim.

Phase 1 reachability: office_pc (192.168.3.2) reached pc2 (128.168.0.2) with
0% loss and ~5 ms RTT. All four Internet Lab hosts (pc2–pc5) reached office_pc
with 0% loss in both directions.

Infrastructure sweep (infra_sweep): zero flagged devices, no ACL/firewall drop
rules, no static ARP anomalies, all seven sampled hosts have valid IPv4
addresses and default routes.

L2 snapshot (l2_snapshot): no real MAC conflicts. The three "duplicate MAC
groups" reported are the null/zero MACs on unused Linux kernel tunnel interfaces
(tunl0, gre0, etc.) that are present identically on every container — a
standard Kathara artefact, not a forwarding issue.

Control plane (Phase B): RIP has converged across all three routers. router1
carries 128.168.0.0/16 via router2 and 192.168.3.0/24 as directly connected;
router2 carries 192.168.3.0/24 via router1; the wan_r1_r2 transit link is
healthy. No routing black-hole exists.

Traffic control (tc_snapshot): all 39 interfaces carry default pfifo_fast
qdiscs with zero flagged shaping or policing.

Resource pressure (pressure_sweep): zero suspect devices across all 30 nodes.

No mechanism — no ACL rule, no flap script, no mis-route, no rate limiter —
can account for the reported outage. The claim is unconfirmed by live evidence
and must be treated as a past transient that has self-resolved, or a false
alarm. No corrective action is warranted.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes the inter-router links are up and the 128.168.0.0/16 Internet Lab prefix is reachable from the Office segment at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirmed the WAN/inter-router link is healthy and that the 128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present and reachable from the Office (office_pc reached pc2 with 0% loss).

The agent's investigation log shows direct reachability tests (0% loss), routing table checks (RIP routes present), L2/TC/pressure scans with no flags, and uses those observations to conclude no current outage — a justified negative-control diagnosis. Evidence in the log supports the key claims and the inferences follow logically with adequate coverage of layers.
